Note on quantities and undertaking Like many others, I have neither written a novel nor read Marcel Proust's In Search of Lost Time (À la recherche du temps perdu). That this undone can become a problem is because of PROUST. From PROUST it follows that novels are no longer something one does. It's straightforward to plan, leaf through, sketch, and skim, but with certain personal characteristics comes the striving for totality, which can rightly be attributed to a PROUST complex. Everything is easy in the work, but to be free, I must turn the whole problem of consciousness: Do I get out, or does PROUST? Therefore, more and more declare that they have read PROUST than those of us who admit that we certainly cannot. When I sometimes hear myself outdone, for here and there having written a novel and read PROUST, I must at least assert that these are splendid individuals who do not blame themselves much, and who therefore have never been accused of not being able to do their work. A way around it all has dawned on me, for with my head intact I should be able to solve the first by writing the second. But in the swap between “æ” and “ø” in read/solve and “the first” and “the second” in write-read there has been a shift in meaning, admittedly quite tautological. Get it written by writing it off? After suitable influence from first Llambias’ unobtrusive rewrite of Brøgger’s love confrontation, then Borges’s classic text about Pierre Menard, who wrote an exact Don Quixote after Cervantes, and then Larsen’s parasite over Christensen’s sonnets, I have chosen to maintain my fundamental claim within a most incorporeal engagement with PROUST. personification, MARCEL PROUST (3-11-8-1-7-10-9-4-12-2-5-13-6). Since the displayed solution is recursive, the question is how the combination of CL and MP can be calculated. What does this mean? The etymology behind COMPUTER LARS alludes to 'triumph of computation.' From LARS via LAURENTIUS via LAURBÆR arises the archaic wreath, which with Apollo’s blessing adorns the honored poet or triumphator. In COMPUTER lies COMPUTATION and hence CALCULATION. The triumph in a 'triumph of computation' describes having achieved something or performed a feat. The triumph does not require that one side wins over the other. For a computation to be honored, it must undertake the undecidable. The computation undertakes the undecidable by prediction. Cf. probability theory, the likelihood of the occurrence of COMPUTER LARS in MARCEL PROUST (rather than OULPR SMARTCE, PMEUCRSA LORT, etc.) can be expressed with a point between 0 and 1. Since the names CL and MP consist of thirteen letters with only one repetition, each combination will occur in one out of three billion cases, specifically [████]. If CL is taken from MP, it is given as one out of [████]. The probability for CL at a given time is therefore 0,000000032 in relation to an MP given as 1 (where MP is 1 due to the historical event MARCEL PROUST). Converted from combinations to seconds to years, given continuous input of ( , A, C, E, L, M, O, P, R, R, S, T, U) a probable recurrence of an arrangement occurs within every 99 years. After MARCEL PROUST's death in 1922, an event is thus open until the end of 2021. The undecidable aspect of a probability, which one can learn from MP, lies in each arrangement's possibility of recognition, recollection, rediscovery, reunion, etc.

In distributional semantics, it is said that a word must be known by its company. Since language is generated by predicting the next word in a series, context can indicate when PROUST comes after MARCEL and LARS after COMPUTER. If a Marcel has written a Recherche, it is probably Marcel Proust, and if a computer has generated honored literature, it is called a computer lars.

In the connection between MP and CL, the context shifts further, since combinatorics links the proper names MARCEL and LARS, while the technical COMPUTER is related to the author PROUST. From these connections, a pair of quasi-antonyms can be formed to concretize the conceptual context, e.g., MAN LARS and ROBO PROUST.

This company, MP-(ML-RP)-CL, constitutes the circle of acquaintances for the connection MP-CL. The function describes the connection routes from MP-CL and CL-MP, e.g.: 1)   MP1-ML1-RP1-CL1   or      2)   MP2-RP2-ML2-CL2 where 2) depends on 1).

For 1) the case is that MARCEL PROUST as a human (MAN LARS) is itself computerized, a ROBO PROUST. Thus, the conditions for COMPUTER LARS to be found in MP (in Recherche) are met. Since CL1 is part of MP1’s work, the concept CL is derived from MP’s function.

For 2) it applies that MARCEL PROUST is a technical construction modeled as a ROBO PROUST by a human programmer MAN LARS, who can then be honored as COMPUTER LARS. Here, CL’s triumph causes the return of a genuine MP. This depends on 1) securing the construction of CL1 through MP1, since MP2 via RP2 otherwise is not a real recurrence but merely a copy, clone, or pastiche.

Derived from the author identity Marcel Proust, the undecidable in the relationship MARCEL PROUST and COMPUTER LARS is concretized in the question of the fate of literature: Who now wears Apollo's laurel wreath, human or machine?1.

LITERARY UNDECIDABILITY (MP1-ML1-RP1-CL1)

According to MARCEL PROUST (cf. Gilles Deleuze), his Recherche is already an apparatus or a machine rather than an organic totality. One cannot choose between human and machine literature, as their respective creation processes have long been indistinguishable. Everything is generated in the time of language, so MARCEL PROUST – in a union of MAN LARS and ROBO PROUST – is behind the first construction of a COMPUTER LARS.

In this way, a technical continuation of PROUST's work is possible if the fundamental condition is fulfilled that one learns to use the apparatus.2.

LITERARY UNDECIDABILITY (MP2-RP2-ML2-CL2)

If PROUST's literary machine is still operable, its statistical level can be learned by a language model. This learning consists of the philosophically difficult derivation of semantics from syntax, meaning from word combinations, significance from sentence formation. In PROUST, this level (again cf. Deleuze) is structured abstractly and erotically, first by heterosexual relations and then by both directions within homosexual relations. Thus, MAN LARS’s concrete, manual modeling of ROBO PROUST should repeat how MP’s syntax, i.e., the sum of words, sentences, and names, produces a meaningful, libidinal relational complex. In that case, the relationship is reversed, and MARCEL PROUST is a derivation of COMPUTER LARS.

How words become what they can do is up to MAN LARS. One must inquire into ML in RP, that is:
WHO IS LARS?
and
WHAT DOES LARS DO?
and
WHERE IS LARS?

LARSWhere did Lars go after having been at Marcel's?…

The probability of identifying MAN LARS suggests that Lars is a white adult man, as almost no children, racialized people, or women are named Lars (0-0,02%). Lars nevertheless dominates demography as an average human, a zoon automaton, who as an exclusive phenomenon from the last millennium primarily takes the shape of leader, cultural figure, or technician, with few exorbitant exceptions. A rough projection indicates half of the existing Larses' continued life after the singularity.

In any case, a Lars is honored by his predictability.
